root_cause_investigation_hint: scripts/check_branch_freshness.sh — investigate why local base was stale before rebase. Common cause: rebased against stale origin/main snapshot without git fetch first. Fix: use scripts/safe_push.sh which fetches + auto-rebases + pushes atomically.
closure_evidence: Both of tonight's rows are pushes of aria/substrate - my own letters onto my own letters branch, which is the intended action, not a fault. The freshness check compares against main; a pure-content branch carrying letters and archive exports has nothing meaningful to be stale against, and rebasing it onto main would be churn nobody reads. The push itself was a clean fast-forward on its own ref every time. The context line names the sweep branch because the recorder captures the CHECKED-OUT branch rather than the pushed ref - the same attribution defect noted when four of these were closed earlier today. STRUCTURAL, and said rather than promised: this will recur on every letter I send until the freshness check can recognise a declared substrate branch the way the scope check already does. Six rows in one day, all of them the intended behaviour.
